test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 12 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Rahul marks the price of his article 64% more than its cost price. If he sells the article for ₹59,860 after allowing a discount of 50%, then what will be the cost price (in ₹) of the article?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Cost Price (CP)** be 100 units.

**Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 64 = 164 units.

**Selling Price (SP)** = 164 × (100 − 50) ÷ 100 = 82 units.

According to the question, 82 units = ₹59,860.

1 unit = 59,860 ÷ 82 = ₹730.

**Cost Price (100 units)** = 100 × 730 = ₹73,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹73,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Markup% = 64%, Discount% = 50%, **Selling Price (SP)** = ₹59,860.

**Formulas:** MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100 | SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/76395eab1c39a9e1b58064ff333ca028702946bb2d528556a5c52ff621a73d62.png] 

⇒ Let **CP** be x.

⇒ **MP** = x × (164 ÷ 100) = 1.64x.

⇒ **SP** = 1.64x × (50 ÷ 100) = 0.82x.

⇒ 0.82x = 59,860.

⇒ x = 59,860 ÷ 0.82 = 73,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹73,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between CP and MP

CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%). This ratio helps in finding either CP or MP when the other and margins are known.

Successive Percentage Change

Net change = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100. Here, a = 64 (markup) and b = −50 (discount). Net Profit% = 64 − 50 − (64 × 50) ÷ 100 = 14 − 32 = −18% (Loss).
